learning: Expect the speed gain to lift oval finish rate and cut completion_time. If off-track exits rise while max_error stays near 0.043 m, the controller is being outrun, and the next step is a mass or track change rather than more speed.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's Iteration 4 geometry: the Iteration 2 design with wheel_radius raised to 0.040 m. The controller is unchanged from Iteration 2 so the race isolates the drivetrain change.
rationale: Iteration 2 is still the best design (score 329, oval finish rate 65%, oval mean finish time 1.80 s). Entity0 changes only wheel_radius, from 0.035 to 0.040 m, and keeps every other geometry field at the Iteration 2 values. Because the sensor layout, track, mass and body are unchanged, the radius change is the only variable in this race. Raising the radius raises ground speed per wheel rotation by about 14%. Iteration 2 showed oval off-track exits (7 of 20) while the finish time left about 1.2 s of margin, so the speed gain is the lever being tested. I keep the Iteration 2 controller exactly (base_speed 1.6, kp 3.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Changing the controller in the same race would confound the test. Weights match the 0.036 m spread via x/0.018, as in Iterations 1 and 2. Expected result: a higher oval finish rate and lower completion_time than Iteration 2. Off-track exits in bends are the main risk, and the telemetry will show whether they rise. Nothing about this robot's performance has been measured yet.
